These dates fall during a perigean spring tide, when the moon will be full and closest to the Earth and approaching the winter solstice, when the sun is at its maximum declination relative to the equator, and Perihelion, when the Earth is closest to the sun. More Kelvin waves are likely to occur throughout the fall and winter due to ongoing El Niño conditions, which would keep water levels elevated. NOAA’s National Weather Service Winter Outlook predicts wetter-than-average conditions for the southwestern U.S. which may further exacerbate coastal flooding along inland coasts where excessive runoff from increased storm activity can further add to already elevated water levels. Communities can use NOAA's Monthly High Tide Flooding Outlook to see what days in the coming weeks-to-months have an increased risk of coastal flooding based on astronomical tides and changes in seasonal patterns. Weather conditions or the effects of El Niño may worsen or cause flooding outside of the dates listed in this product. Communities should refer to the National Weather Service for the most up-to-date coastal flood forecasts, advisories, and warnings. During a flood event, communities can use NOAA's Coastal Inundation Dashboard to monitor water levels in real-time.
